statements.text: In February, for example, a pregnant black woman was wrongfully arrested for robbery and carjacking due to a mistaken result from facial recognition technology. [...] As companies adopt complex algorithms to make critical decisions on everything from housing to consumer prices, the Federal Trade Commission must keep a very close eye on this conduct and ensure algorithmic discrimination does not become a feature of our marketplace.
statements.context: Senate Commerce Committee nomination hearing for FTC and CPSC nominees, where Senator Markey warns about algorithmic discrimination and AI-amplified harms.

statements.text: I also want to discuss the hottest topic in Washington, artificial intelligence. We are having an AI moment, but data privacy, protection from bias, algorithms, and algorithmic justice are not new topics.
statements.context: Senator Markey questions nominees at a Senate Commerce Committee hearing on FTC and CPSC nominations, pivoting from children's privacy to AI and algorithmic bias.

statements.text: So these data centers are using scarce water supplies across our country for cooling these chips. [...] the energy required to power this technology is contributing to the biggest problem of them all, climate change.
statements.context: Senate hearing on Chips and Science Act implementation, featuring Senator Markey questioning Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo on AI sustainability.

statements.text: with AI, every one of them might have it individualized with their home language, ability to be able to give them that kind of individualized attention that they need.
statements.context: Senator Markey speaks at a field hearing in Lowell, Massachusetts, on the economic impact of federal investments.

statements.text: As Ranking Member of the HELP Committee, I'm focused on ensuring that we are prepared for the continued deployment of AI.
statements.context: Senate HELP Subcommittee hearing record on AI in health care, including Senator Markey's written policy framework document submitted as additional material.

statements.text: That is true, if not carefully implemented with Government oversight and worker input, AI can harm health care workers by making them feel like the art and science of health care is distilled to typing into an iPad, and that is all there will be to it.
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI in health care, Senator Markey questioning a witness on workplace impacts.

statements.text: We have learned time and again that left to self-regulate, big tech puts profit over people almost every time. [...] Unregulated experimentation involving artificial intelligence may fuel our next pandemic. [...] Humans insert human bias and discrimination into algorithms that can supercharge existing inequalities in our health care system, jeopardize our privacy, and misdiagnose or mistreat patients.
statements.context: Opening statement by Senator Markey at a Senate HELP Subcommittee hearing on AI in health care.

statements.text: Ms. Huberty, what do stories like Jim's, that you told us here, tell us about insurance companies and companies developing artificial intelligence, and how they are incorporating patient experience versus their profit motivation? Can you talk about the lesson we should learn from that experience?
statements.context: Senate subcommittee hearing on AI in health care, during the question-and-answer portion led by Senator Markey.

statements.text: Yes. And who should bear the burden of proving that the use of artificial intelligence won't harm patients? Where should that burden of proof lie?
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI in health care, during a Q&A exchange with a witness.

statements.text: I introduced which Senator Budd, Republican on this Committee, the Artificial Intelligence and Biosecurity Risk Assessment Act, and the Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats Act to direct the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to prepare for AI biosecurity threats.
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI in health care, during the Q&A portion where Senator Markey questions expert witnesses.

statements.text: So the hearings I had in the 1990s were on AI and how AI is going to be used in order to do all of this targeting. [...] Similarly, the law does not contain strict protections against excessive data collection or targeted advertising by Big Tech.
statements.context: Senator Ed Markey speaks on the Senate floor during debate on the Children and Teen's Online Privacy Protection Act.

statements.text: With AI supercharging Big Tech's algorithms and encouraging platforms to collect more data on young people, it has never been more important to protect our young people's privacy.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks during the executive session on the Kids Online Safety Act and COPPA 2.0.

statements.text: That is why yesterday I introduced my AI Civil Rights Act of 2024, comprehensive legislation that would prevent discriminatory algorithms from being used in critical decisions, including employment, because we cannot prepare our workforce without protecting our workers simultaneously.
statements.context: Senate hearing titled "Reading the Room: Preparing Workers for AI".

statements.text: Algorithms that match candidates with job opportunities that refer more to men than women for open roles.
statements.context: Senator Markey delivers opening remarks at a Senate hearing on AI workforce preparation.

statements.text: That is why my AI Civil Rights Act would require companies to test these algorithms for discriminatory impact before their use, preventing biased AI from being incorporated into resumes screening, job recommendations, worker performance, and even health care decisions.
statements.context: Senate hearing titled "Reading the Room: Preparing Workers for AI," where Senator Markey advocates for algorithmic accountability and clean-energy AI.

statements.text: That is unacceptable. We cannot let AI stand for accelerating inequality and it is why in September, I introduced the AI Civil Rights Act which would ensure that companies review and eliminate bias in their algorithms and put Americans back in control of key decisions in their lives.
statements.context: Senate hearing on protecting consumers from AI-enabled fraud and scams, where Senator Markey advocates for his AI Civil Rights Act.

statements.text: Because these issues now are well documented. In fact, in 2021 both AARP and the Federal Trade Commission published reports that determined that Black and Latino adults were more likely to be targeted by scammers and by fraudsters. As artificial intelligence gives these bad actors new tools to target the public, communities of color will inevitably be the most impacted.
statements.context: Senator Markey questions a witness during a Senate hearing on protecting consumers from AI-enabled fraud and scams.

statements.text: We have to take action against the companies that set up these algorithms. So as Congress considers AI legislation we just cannot ignore how those algorithms will impact marginalized communities and that is why we have to pass my AI Civil Rights Act [...]
statements.context: Verbatim remarks by Senator Markey during a hearing on protecting consumers from AI-enabled fraud and scams.

statements.text: Our witnesses today have done a very effective job in demonstrating that artificial intelligence poses serious new risks for fraud and scams across different sectors. From AI voice cloning tools to deepfake images and videos AI is threatening to undermine our ability to tell truth from falsity, to sow distrust in our understanding of reality itself.
statements.context: Senator Markey delivers opening remarks at a Senate hearing on protecting consumers from AI-enabled fraud and scams.

statements.text: This is unacceptable. That is why, in September, I introduced my AI Civil Rights Act, comprehensive legislation intended to ensure that the AI age does not replicate and supercharge the bias and discrimination already prevalent today in our real world.
statements.context: Senate floor speech during an Executive Session on Artificial Intelligence, where Senator Markey announced new endorsements for his AI Civil Rights Act.

statements.text: We need treaties that end the nuclear arms race. We don't need a nuclear arms race with AI making these weapons even more deadly, even more accurate. We need treaties. We need negotiations. We need to come together on the planet. That is what we should be talking about.
statements.context: Senate floor speech during Executive Session on the nomination of Pete Hegseth as Secretary of Defense.

statements.text: AI has infiltrated every sector of our economy. [...] But we also have to make sure that the AI age does not supercharge preexisting bias and discrimination in our society using super algorithms to look at people in our society and then make it easier to discriminate against them.
statements.context: Senator Markey questions Howard Lutnick during his Commerce Secretary nomination hearing, pivoting from contract obligations to AI's societal risks.

statements.text: So that is why this Congress introduced the ``Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impact Act'' to study both the positive and negative consequences of AI. [...] Yes, AI might find—may find a cure for cancer. It may, but AI also could help to contribute to a climate disaster. That is also equally true. So we need to just keep both of those things right on the table [...] We are talking about technology used to calculate a family's mortgage, screen an individual's job application, and determine a senior's medical care. When used in these situations it is absolutely essential that AI-powered algorithms are free from bias and discrimination.
statements.context: Senator Markey delivers opening remarks at a Senate hearing on U.S. computing and AI innovation capabilities.

statements.text: Do you think it would be helpful for the government to convene stakeholders including from industry and academia to help better measure AI's environmental impact?
statements.context: Senate hearing titled 'Winning the AI Race: Strengthening U.S. Capabilities in Computing and Innovation' on May 8, 2025.

statements.text: The massive data centers that are critical for AI development requires substantial amounts of electricity, putting stress on the grid and potentially raising costs for consumers.
statements.context: Senate hearing on strengthening U.S. AI and computing capabilities, where Senator Markey shifts focus to AI's environmental costs.

statements.text: My question is should the Federal Government be on an ongoing basis studying the impact of AI?
statements.context: Senate hearing titled 'Winning the AI Race: Strengthening U.S. Capabilities in Computing and Innovation'.

statements.text: We do not need to wait and see if poorly tested and trained algorithms will harm marginalized communities. Artificial intelligence is already supercharging the bias and discrimination prevalent in our society.
statements.context: Senate hearing titled 'Winning the AI Race: Strengthening U.S. Capabilities in Computing and Innovation,' where Senator Markey questions a witness and advocates for his proposed AI Civil Rights Act.

statements.text: A recent analysis found that American's electricity bills are going to rise by as much as 25 percent over the next 4 years—25 percent because of data center demand. [...] So Mr. Kratsios, do you think it is appropriate that the Administration is forcing Americans to pay more on their electricity bills, while using their taxpayer dollars to make the even worse by funding the unfettered growth of the AI industry?
statements.context: Senate hearing titled "AI've Got a Plan: America's AI Action Plan," featuring Senator Markey questioning a witness on AI policy impacts.

statements.text: Is that a violation? Does that qualify as ideological bias and should xAI therefore be disqualified from Federal contracts?
statements.context: Senator Markey questions a witness during a hearing on America's AI Action Plan, citing a Grok output as evidence of ideological bias.

statements.text: Would that be a violation of the rule that a generative AI system, if it is stated that it intentionally trained to adopt a political viewpoint? Would that qualify as a top-down ideological bias?
statements.context: Senate hearing on America's AI Action Plan, where Senator Markey questions a witness about ideological bias in AI training.

statements.text: This language is extraordinarily vague, ``free from the top-down ideological bias,'' and it gives the Trump Administration vast discretion to force AI chat box developers to adopt conservative viewpoints or else risk losing lucrative Federal contracts.
statements.context: Senate hearing on the America's AI Action Plan, where Senator Markey questions Director Kratsios about energy policy and AI procurement language.

statements.text: this Administration is giving AI data centers the green light to eat up our electricity in our Nation while our bank accounts go into the red. So Mr. Kratsios, are you aware of how much households' electricity bills are expected to rise over the next 4 years as a result of data center expansion?
statements.context: Senate hearing titled "AI've Got a Plan: America's AI Action Plan," Senator Markey questioning a witness on AI data-center energy costs.

statements.text: So I want to turn to a technology that poses new risks to kids, AI chatbots. Tens of millions of teens across the country are using AI chatbots to answer questions, find companionship, practice social skills, and although AI chatbots may have some benefits I am deeply concerned that Big Tech companies will implement the same profitable, exploitative formula to AI chatbots as they have done with social media.
statements.context: Senate hearing on technology's impact on youth, where Senator Markey shifts from social media privacy to AI chatbot risks.
